The design's whole value is contact depth, bought by a lug trim at r_trim = farthest flank contact + trim_wall 1.5 mm, with the contact read at the lug's MID-PLANE (model line 86; row name, doc and dashboard say '+ 1.5 mm wall'). The gen-7 CAD check (docs/research/user_slipper_nose_fix_check.md O2, lines 176-187) reads the same contact line at the lug's TOP edge (+1.5 mm along ez): farthest contact 20.22 mm over [0, dK_lim 49.75] and 20.48 mm over the built 51.75-deg stroke, so the wall the built part keeps past the last contact is 1.08 / 0.82 mm, not 1.5. The verifier's trim check T1 reads 2.53 / 1.99 mm on its own construction (rings +-1.25 mm along the GH ruling): the two independent readings disagree. Measured here, model unchanged, only trim_wall varied (tools/alignment_trimlug_edgewall.py): with the 1.5 mm wall kept at the top edge (trim_wall 1.95 -> r_trim 21.72; 2.21 -> 21.98) the frozen exact gap is 18.50 at 2.21 (claim 18.51; score-neutral), but bench T5 rises 13.18 -> 13.44 / 13.70 mm (pose 264: 4.18 -> 4.44 / 4.70; the lead 5.74) and the 10 held-out contacts 40.59 -> 41.85 / 42.89 mm (the lead with the same dense lug 46.35). So 0.26-0.52 of the 1.56 mm bench depth gain (17-33 %) and 1.26-2.30 of the 5.76 mm held gain (22-40 %) is metal cut out of the stated wall at the lug's top edge. Not gamed: the score is blind to depth (it charges +0.02 for the trim), the design ranks behind its parent, no wall rule exists, and the MVP1 nose load (5-15 N) is trivial for 0.8 mm. It is a margin stated on one plane of a 3-D part.
